description: Apply the UTC range conversion from ArgentinaTimeZone (FEAT-001) in all backend date-range query sites so UTC-stored timestamps are compared against ranges derived from Argentine local filter dates. Covers the four history repositories and the report/dashboard ranges. Depends on FEAT-001. This is the fix that makes the night sale reappear in the history.
steps: src/SistemaAlmacen.Data/Repositories/VentaRepository.cs (GetHistorialAsync): replace the FechaInicio/FechaFin Where blocks (including `var fechaFinInclusive = filter.FechaFin.Value.Date.AddDays(1).AddTicks(-1)`) with `var (inicioUtc, finUtc) = ArgentinaTimeZone.ToUtcRange(filter.FechaInicio, filter.FechaFin);` then `query = query.Where(v => v.Fecha >= inicioUtc && v.Fecha <= finUtc);`. Add `using SistemaAlmacen.Shared.Common;` and a brief comment citing the convention.
src/SistemaAlmacen.Data/Repositories/CajaRepository.cs (GetHistorialCierresAsync): same replacement but filter on c.FechaCierre (currently compares raw `>= FechaInicio` / `<= FechaFin`).

src/SistemaAlmacen.Data/Repositories/AuditoriaRepository.cs (GetHistorialAsync): same replacement on a.Fecha (currently compares raw bounds); leave UsuarioId/TipoOperacion/EntidadAfectada filters untouched.

src/SistemaAlmacen.Business/Services/ReporteService.cs: in GenerarReporteVentasAsync and GenerarReporteProductosAsync, replace `var inicio = fechaInicio.Date;` / `var fin = fechaFin.Date.AddDays(1).AddTicks(-1);` with `var (inicio, fin) = ArgentinaTimeZone.ToUtcRange(fechaInicio, fechaFin);` keeping the existing `v.Fecha >= inicio && v.Fecha <= fin` comparisons. Keep ValidarRangoFechas as-is.

ReporteService.GenerarReporteVentasAsync DesgloseDiario: change `.GroupBy(v => v.Fecha.Date)` to `.GroupBy(v => ArgentinaTimeZone.ToLocal(v.Fecha).Date)` so daily buckets are Argentine-local days (safe: grouping runs in memory on the materialized list).

ReporteService.GenerarDashboardAsync: replace `var ahora = DateTime.Now;` with `var ahora = ArgentinaTimeZone.ToLocal(DateTime.UtcNow);`. Compute local inicioHoy/finHoy and inicioMes/finMes from `ahora`, then convert each boundary pair to UTC before querying UTC v.Fecha — reuse ArgentinaTimeZone.ToUtcRange(inicioHoy, inicioHoy) for the day and ToUtcRange(inicioMes.Date, finMes.Date) for the month (or convert the boundaries directly with the same helper semantics). Ensure all four Where clauses (ventasHoy, ventasMes, topProductos, and any detalle query) use the UTC boundaries.

ReporteService GenerarPdf header 'al {DateTime.Now:dd/MM/yyyy}': change DateTime.Now to ArgentinaTimeZone.ToLocal(DateTime.UtcNow) for consistency. Add `using SistemaAlmacen.Shared.Common;` to ReporteService.cs.
acceptance_criteria: No repository or ReporteService date-range path still uses `.Date.AddDays(1).AddTicks(-1)` against a UTC column, nor DateTime.Now/DateTime.Today for range computation (FacturacionService is untouched).
VentaRepository/CompraRepository/CajaRepository/AuditoriaRepository each derive their range from ArgentinaTimeZone.ToUtcRange.
dotnet test SistemaAlmacen.slnx passes (FEAT-001 helper tests still green).
verification: Run `dotnet build SistemaAlmacen.slnx` and confirm success.
Run `dotnet test SistemaAlmacen.slnx` and confirm all tests pass.
findings:
All backend date-range sites now derive their UTC range from ArgentinaTimeZone.ToUtcRange (namespace SistemaAlmacen.Shared.Common). Changes made:
- VentaRepository.GetHistorialAsync, CompraRepository.GetHistorialAsync, CajaRepository.GetHistorialCierresAsync (filters c.FechaCierre, which is DateTime? — the `>= inicioUtc && <= finUtc` comparison compiles/runs fine as it did before), AuditoriaRepository.GetHistorialAsync: each replaced the old FechaInicio/FechaFin Where blocks with `var (inicioUtc, finUtc) = ArgentinaTimeZone.ToUtcRange(filter.FechaInicio, filter.FechaFin); query = query.Where(x => x.Fecha >= inicioUtc && x.Fecha <= finUtc);` (FechaCierre for Caja). Added `using SistemaAlmacen.Shared.Common;` to all four.
- ReporteService.cs: added `using SistemaAlmacen.Shared.Common;`. GenerarReporteVentasAsync and GenerarReporteProductosAsync now use `var (inicio, fin) = ArgentinaTimeZone.ToUtcRange(fechaInicio, fechaFin);` (ValidarRangoFechas unchanged). DesgloseDiario groups by `ArgentinaTimeZone.ToLocal(v.Fecha).Date` (in-memory on materialized list), so DesgloseDiarioDto.Fecha is now an Argentine-local day — relevant for FEAT-003 if the client needs to display it (it is already a local date, do NOT re-convert). GenerarDashboardAsync: `ahora = ArgentinaTimeZone.ToLocal(DateTime.UtcNow)`; local inicioMesLocal/finMesLocal computed from ahora; day range via ToUtcRange(ahora.Date, ahora.Date) and month range via ToUtcRange(inicioMesLocal, finMesLocal); all Where clauses (ventasHoy, ventasMes, topProductos) use the UTC bounds. GenerarPdf header 'al ...' now uses ArgentinaTimeZone.ToLocal(DateTime.UtcNow).
- No remaining `.Date.AddDays(1).AddTicks(-1)` against UTC columns and no DateTime.Now/DateTime.Today for range computation in these files. FacturacionService intentionally untouched.
For FEAT-003 (Blazor display): repositories/API now return UTC Venta.Fecha etc. as before (values stored UTC, Kind=Unspecified). The client still formats these raw via ToString("dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm") WITHOUT converting to local, so displayed times remain off by the UTC offset until FEAT-003 wraps display values in ArgentinaTimeZone.ToLocal(...). Filter dates continue to be sent as yyyy-MM-dd local days (no client change needed for filtering — the backend now interprets them as Argentine-local). Verification: dotnet build + dotnet test both pass (25 tests, 0 failures).
